question.knowledge_point: Using Alternative Forms of Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions
question.problem: Express $\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{2}{sin}^{2}⁡{55}^{∘}$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
question.worked_solution:
Our expression can be factored as follows:

$$
\sqrt{2}(1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{55}^{∘})
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={55}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{55}^{∘} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {55}^{∘})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{110}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}(1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{55}^{∘}) & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{110}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
